tools.name: pixel_help
tools.description: Start here before drawing pixel art, sprites, tiles, icons, effects or animations. Returns a short quick start: the recipe format, the operations, the tools and the workflow. Pass a topic only when you need more: presets (ready-made fire, smoke, explosions, spells, characters and more to compile instead of drawing), preset with name (one preset's source), guide (the full authoring reference and every tool option), workflow (art workflow: poses, scenes, particles, fluids, lighting), schema (the recipe JSON Schema), example (a complete recipe), or poses, scenes, autotile, fx, fluid, wave or normals for those source formats' schemas.

tools.name: pixel_validate
tools.description: Check a pixel art recipe for mistakes before inspecting or exporting it. Returns its revision id, size, frame timing, animations and clipping, without images or files.

project.description: A version-1 Pixelbolt recipe: {"version": 1, "name", "width", "height", "palette", "symbols"?, "frames": [{"name", "duration"?, "from"?, "ops"?, "layers"?}], "animations"?}; see pixel_help.

revision.description: Revision id from an earlier response, sent instead of project.

fps.description: Also check timing against a video frame rate (24, 25, "29.97", 30, 60 or a fraction): frameGrid lists durations off the grid.

tools.name: pixel_inspect
tools.description: Look at pixel art, a sprite or an animation frame by frame to check how it looks, without exporting. Returns a PNG contact sheet of every frame (or the chosen frames, or one animation in playback order) with each cell's name and duration. grid: true adds palette-key text grids for exact pixels, region zooms in, and view picks a tile, onion or motion review. Use this while iterating; call pixel_render to export.

guides.description: Perspective guides: {horizon: row, vanish: [[x, y], …up to 3], iso: {tile: [32, 16], at: [x, y]}}.

project.description: A version-1 Pixelbolt recipe: {"version": 1, "name", "width", "height", "palette", "symbols"?, "frames": [{"name", "duration"?, "from"?, "ops"?, "layers"?}], "animations"?}; see pixel_help.

revision.description: Revision id from an earlier response, sent instead of project.

source.description: A pixelforge-poses source instead of project/revision, for motion review with its contacts.

metadata.description: Pose metadata from pixel_compile (metadata: true), for motion review of a compiled revision.

reference.description: Revision to compare against: adds a before/after image and the changed pixels.

frames.description: Frame names to show, in order; * and ? match, as in "flash-*". Default: every frame.

animation.description: Show one animation in playback order instead of frames.

region.description: Crop every frame to this canvas rectangle.

grid.description: Also return palette-key text grids with x/y rulers (at most 16,384 pixels).

scale.description: Contact sheet scale. Default: the largest that fits about 1024 px.

background.description: checker (default), transparent, a palette name or a hex color.

view.description: onion and motion need animation; motion reports foot slide, ground error and loop joins (source or metadata adds contacts); tile repeats each frame 3x3.

diagnostics.description: Advisory evidence: duplicate and empty frames, stray pixels, palette, loop joins, timing, cleanup counts.

maxCells.description: Show at most this many evenly spaced cells; step and offset pick positions instead.

step.description: Keep every step-th cell from offset; step 2 shows the A frames of an A/B strobe.

tools.name: pixel_patch
tools.description: Fix or tweak pixel art (one pixel, a colour, a frame or its timing) without redrawing it. Pass revision or project plus changes applied in order, such as {"set": "frames[blink].duration", "value": 120} or {"paint": "frames[blink]", "value": [{"x": 9, "y": 7, "color": "k"}]}; other paths look like palette.k or frames[blink].layers[body].ops[2].x2. The patch is atomic and must validate. Returns the new revision, every frame whose pixels changed and a before/after PNG.

project.description: A version-1 Pixelbolt recipe: {"version": 1, "name", "width", "height", "palette", "symbols"?, "frames": [{"name", "duration"?, "from"?, "ops"?, "layers"?}], "animations"?}; see pixel_help.

revision.description: Revision id from an earlier response, sent instead of project.

changes.description: Edits applied in order. Paths match error paths, such as frames[3].duration; lists also accept [name] and [-] to append.

set.description: Path to replace, or an object field to add.

insert.description: List position to insert before; [-] appends.

remove.description: Object field or list item to delete.

paint.description: Frame path such as frames[blink]; value: [{x, y, color}] canvas pixels after all layers (transparent erases).

grid.description: Frame path; value: {x, y, rows, erase?, mask?}, dots keep pixels.

move.description: Frame path; value: {x, y, w, h, dx, dy, mask?}.

recolor.description: Frame path; value: {x, y, w, h, from, to, mask?}.

cleanup.description: Frame path; value: {corners?, strays?, x?, y?, w?, h?, mask?, colors?}. Proposes fixes for doubled corners and stray pixels; check the report.

scope.description: Canvas edits: inherited (default), or frame to leave frames that inherit it unchanged.

overlay.description: A saved pixelforge-overlay to apply instead of changes.

tools.name: pixel_render
tools.description: Export pixel art as game-ready files: sprite sheet, sprites, animations, GIFs or frames for a video. Writes a PNG sheet, atlas JSON, Godot 4 SpriteFrames (and a TileSet for an autotile set), frame PNGs, APNGs, CSS and a Canvas player to a new folder in the export directory, and returns the key files, a check of what was delivered and a contact sheet. Pass expect with what the user asked for, then fix every problem the check lists before handing the files on. Pass saveAs to also write files where the user asked.

project.description: A version-1 Pixelbolt recipe: {"version": 1, "name", "width", "height", "palette", "symbols"?, "frames": [{"name", "duration"?, "from"?, "ops"?, "layers"?}], "animations"?}; see pixel_help.

revision.description: Revision id from an earlier response, sent instead of project.

animation.description: Preview this animation in playback order; every animation is exported either way.

listFiles.description: List every exported file, not only the key ones.

scale.description: Default 1, the frames' own size; enlarge only for posting.

background.description: Palette name or opaque hex to blend onto. Default: 1-bit transparency.

gif.description: Also write each animation as a GIF in gifs/ ({} for defaults): exact colours, at most 256 per frame.

sequence.description: Also write numbered PNG frames with alpha for a video editor into sequence/, with the ffmpeg command for a .mov.

animation.description: Default: the previewed animation, or the first.

step.description: Video frames per sampled frame; 2 animates on twos.

size.description: 720p, 1080p, 1440p, 4k, vertical, square or WIDTHxHEIGHT. Default: the sprite at scale.

offset.description: [x, y] added to the aligned position.

background.description: Palette name or opaque hex. Default: transparent.

share.description: Also return a playground link that reopens this recipe in a browser.

embedRecipe.description: Embed the recipe in the exported PNGs so they reopen in the playground.

expect.description: What the user asked for: frame size, frames per animation, at most colors, a transparent background, loop, GIF scale. The reply's check lists each miss and the call that fixes it.

saveAs.description: Also write files where the user asked, relative to the server root: {"sheet"|"atlas"|"godot"|"tileset"|"recipe"|"gif"|"apng" or a listed file such as "gifs/walk.gif": "assets/hero.png"}. A GIF here implies gif: {}.

overwrite.description: Let saveAs replace existing files. Default: refuse.

tools.name: pixel_compile
tools.description: Build a character animation from parts (with idle, walk, run, jump, attack and hurt templates, squash and tweens), a terrain tileset, particle effects (sparks, embers, dust, a sprite dissolving or teleporting away pixel by pixel) and spell shapes (slashes, shockwave rings, beams, lightning, magic circles, impact stars, fireballs, cel water streams and drops, auras hugging a sprite, smears trailing a sword tip), simulated smoke, fire, explosions, steam, magic swirls, water (splashes, waterfalls, drips, bubbling potions) and thick liquids (honey, slime, mud), coherent interference and portal loops, or a lighting normal map. Compiles the source into an ordinary recipe revision and returns a contact sheet; metadata: true adds pose joints, contacts and timing, the autotile mask table, particle counts, fluid figures, wave counts or normal directions.

source.description: A pixelforge-poses, pixelforge-autotile, pixelforge-fx, pixelforge-fluid, pixelforge-wave or pixelforge-normals document (see pixel_help topics). A normals source's recipe, or an fx symbol's {recipe, frame}, may be inline, a file under the server root or {"revision": id}.

preset.description: Instead of source: a shipped preset by name, such as "smoke-puff" (pixel_help topic presets).

annotations.title: Compile poses, tilesets, effects or fluids

tools.name: pixel_scene
tools.description: Compose a pixel art scene or room from sprites, tilemaps and lighting. Renders a pixelforge-scene manifest (placements, autotiled tilemaps, cues, motion, ground sorting, camera and parallax, haze, lights and shadows; pixel_help topic scenes) at a time in milliseconds and returns the image, placements, lights and warnings. Assets may be inline recipes, files under the server root or {"revision": id}. view: depth shows who covers whom; export: true writes a replayable scene bundle.

guides.description: Perspective guides: {horizon: row, vanish: [[x, y], …up to 3], iso: {tile: [32, 16], at: [x, y]}}.

sequence.description: Also write numbered PNG frames for a video editor: pixel_render's sequence options, without animation and step.

tools.name: pixel_import
tools.description: Turn existing pixel art or a sprite sheet PNG into an editable recipe. Import a native-resolution PNG (RGB, RGBA, greyscale or indexed, up to 8 bits per channel; optionally sliced by an unscaled atlas) as an editable recipe without changing any pixel. Pass data (base64 PNG) or path (inside the server root). Saves the recipe as a revision.

path.description: PNG file path relative to the server root.

annotations.title: Import a PNG as a recipe
